stem:
Anaya gently warms a beaker of pond water that holds dissolved oxygen. She does not add or remove any gas herself.

Which claim correctly predicts what happens to the dissolved oxygen?

options.text: Warming the water tends to drive dissolved oxygen out, so less oxygen stays dissolved.
The amount of dissolved oxygen stays high even when the water is warmed, because gases always stay dissolved.
Warming changes only the colour of the water; dissolved oxygen stays the same.
Warming turns all dissolved oxygen into solid oxygen that settles on the bottom.

teacher.key_rationale: Warming water reduces how much gas such as oxygen stays dissolved. Claiming more dissolves without the temperature condition, that only colour changes, or that oxygen becomes a solid miss that solubility hinge.
